This fixture is independently compiled twice from ordinary TSX `pcbPath`: once with a single authored via, once with explicit colocated wire contacts around that via. No points are removed or routing geometry substituted. Both describe the same 3 mm TOP wire, 2 mm BOTTOM wire, standard 10 kΩ 0603 resistors R1 and R2, with the route connecting actual pads R1.1 and R2.2, and emitted TOP-to-BOTTOM via on a four-layer board.

The repository's existing direct Core dependency resolves to 0.0.1930. The identical TSX was also compiled with published Core 0.0.2125: it retains the same three/five route points and the current checker again reports one error for compact encoding versus none for the contact-expanded control. Copper length in the comparison is measured from actual nonzero segments; the older compiler's `trace_length` field is not the comparison metric.

Current checks 0.0.247 rejects the compact input because its interior-via loop compares both neighboring wire coordinates against the via and requires differences below 0.01 mm. Nonzero wire-to-via and via-to-wire edges are valid authored geometry, so that requirement reports a false `misaligned_via` error. All four 0.8 × 0.95 mm footprint pads remain in the compiled circuit. The snapshot draws the actual emitted footprint pads and silk, compiled copper and labels the actual public checker results.

Related open [#232](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/232) detects disconnected via transitions and physical layer-span mismatches while deliberately retaining the same coordinate-alignment requirement. It does not address this valid compact encoding. [#381](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/381) concerns onward copper at terminal via landings. Neither is a duplicate of this interior compact-route false rejection. Searches for compact and misaligned found no existing PR for this case.

The fix validates the adjoining layer for each nonzero compact edge. Colocated contact wires can reach intermediate layers within a through-via's physical span. If an owned materialized via is present, its actual layer list is authoritative over route-span metadata. Safety controls include an authored blind via ending on the wrong pad layer; explicit invalid incoming/outgoing layer declarations; a narrowed physical barrel with stale full-stack route metadata; and a displaced compiled end pad/port. These deliberately invalid controls are separate from the untouched reproduction/control inputs. Classifier controls also check reversed direction and colocated inner-layer contact. Endpoint and whole-net algorithms are unchanged.

Two older coordinate-only assertions describe physically present short wire/via legs. They now accept that copper. The displaced-pad fixture still reports its genuinely missing pad connection. This patch does not add consecutive-via or terminal-via validation from the related PRs.
